subject.title: Durable Core PR 6/6: add read-only durable inspection

question: Should OpenClaw core adopt the proposed opt-in durable runtime and its public `durable.*` Gateway plus `openclaw durable` operator surface, or should this capability be narrowed or kept outside the current core roadmap?
rationale: The branch is technically substantial but introduces a new cross-owner runtime, configuration, persisted-state, recovery, CLI, and protocol contract; that permanent product boundary cannot be selected safely from implementation evidence alone.

options.title: Pause for architecture sponsorship
options.body: Hold this cumulative PR until maintainers decide the durable-core boundary and the intended staged landing plan.

options.title: Sponsor a narrowed core series
options.body: Accept a specifically bounded durable-core contract, then require rebased incremental PRs that make configuration, upgrade, owner authority, and inspection API commitments explicit.

options.title: Keep recovery with existing owners
options.body: Decline a shared durable layer and direct any remaining gaps to existing task, flow, subagent, session, and delivery-owner APIs.

recommendation.title: Pause for architecture sponsorship
recommendation.body: Hold this cumulative PR until maintainers decide the durable-core boundary and the intended staged landing plan.

likelyOwner.reason: The active stack author can supply the intended boundary and respond to maintainer direction, although upstream ownership is not established by the supplied history.
